title: Regression metrics: MAE, RMSE, MAPE and R²

videos.script: Five minutes off, on average. {{five}} That sounds like the end of the story about a delivery model. It is the start. {{start}} Four metrics judge the same predictions, and they disagree about which model is best. {{disagree}} The mean absolute error rewards the typical delivery. {{mae}} The root mean squared error spends its attention on a flat tyre. {{rmse}} The percentage error quietly prefers predictions that are too low. {{mape}} And R squared depends on the deliveries as much as on the model. {{r2}} Then the question all four ignore. Late, or early? {{direction}} The best model by the usual measure is late on half its promises. {{half}} A promise is a quantile, and a model can be asked for one directly. {{quantile}} By the end, you choose an error the way you chose a cut, from what each mistake costs. {{end}}
